historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle nominal growth. Revenue 5yr CAGR ~1% (FY20 398.7 -> FY25 418.5) plus guided FY27 price increases (5% AU, 4% NZ) against ~2% lower building activity; equity CAGR (1.6%) is not a growth anchor because GWA pays out 85-95% of NPAT and bought back stock.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (-0.1%) diverges from EPS 3yr CAGR (7.2%) by more than 30%: retained earnings are ~nil under the 85-95% payout, so book value carries no growth signal. Revenue and normalised NPAT (0.7% 5yr) are the honest picture: a low-growth, price-and-mix business.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series is lease-adjusted (reported FCF less lease principal and lease interest; FY20-21 lease interest estimated at ~2.9/2.7m from the liability balance): FY20 37.4, FY21 61.8, FY22 -0.8, FY23 57.3, FY24 56.0, FY25 52.4. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is null because the FY22 base is ~zero (working-capital build year, OCF 14.0m); the 5yr figure (7.0%) is flattered by the FY20 COVID-year base. Mid-cycle owner FCF is ~$52-57m, ~12.5-13.5% of revenue. SBC is immaterial so the owner and reported series differ only by the lease deduction (~3.3% of revenue).

scenario_narratives.base: Low-growth price-and-mix compounder: FY27 flat-ish on a soft Australian renovation market, a modest volume recovery FY29-31 as rates ease, EBITDA margin held in the 22-22.5% band it has occupied for six years, ~$52-68m of owner FCF a year after lease cash, mostly paid out. Value is dominated by the terminal (capped at 14x FCF), so the stock is priced on whether the margin band holds.
scenario_narratives.bull: Renovation cycle turns up from FY28, price sticks, UK and the new water-management products add growth, margin edges to 23.5% on operating leverage. Requires several independent things to go right (rates, housing, product adoption), so it carries only a 25% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: Extended downturn plus private-label disintermediation: revenue shrinks two years running, margin compresses to 19.5%, cash conversion stays weak and net debt stays elevated. Management's own FY27 framing (~2% lower building activity, weaker H2 FY26) makes this a live path, hence 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value GWA as a mature, asset-light Australian building-products distributor: a 10-year owner-FCF DCF with leases charged as operating cost, SBC immaterial, a single AUD WACC across scenarios, and a 12-14x terminal cap so the valuation does not lean on Gordon growth. The scenario weights, not the discount rate, carry the housing-cycle risk. The stock's high payout means value accrues as fully franked dividends and buybacks rather than reinvestment.
key_risks_to_valuation: Australian renovation and new-housing cycle: ~60% of Australian revenue is R&R and management already guides FY27 activity down ~2%; a deeper or longer downturn is the bear path
Channel concentration: Reece and other merchants are both customer and private-label competitor; margin band (22-22.5%) is the single most valuable assumption
Working capital and leverage: net debt rose $43m in FY26 on inventory pull-forward; if conversion stays below 80% the buyback and dividend pace slows
Input costs and FX: USD-priced product with only ~55% hedged, plus $3-4m FY27 ocean freight, must be recovered through price without losing volume
Anchor vintage: net debt and share count are the Aug-2026 announced/estimated 30-Jun-2026 figures; the FY2026 annual report is not yet extracted and should replace them
Terminal value is ~half of EV and sits on a 14x FCF cap; GWA has traded at 16-22x owner FCF in better years and ~12x today

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1.94-2.74
data_sources.financials: GWA.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, AUD millions) FY2016-FY2025 annuals and H1 FY2016-H1 FY2026 halves; component lines from GWA.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt (lease principal line 3134, lease interest 3113/3644, ROU depreciation 4463, receivables/inventory/payables 3042-3063, tax paid 3120, diluted shares 3847) and GWA.AX_HalfYear_H1-FY2026.txt (shares outstanding line 650, buyback 507, lease lines 403/422)
data_sources.qualitative: GWA.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-22), including the Aug-2026 FY2026 result summary (revenue 422.3, normalised EBIT 78.2, net debt 127.9, cash conversion 76%, FY27 outlook) sourced by the qualitative analyst via web search and used as directional context and for FY0 revenue / net debt anchors

inputs.base_revenue_source: FY2026 full-year result announced Aug-2026 (revenue $422.3m, +0.9%), per Analysis.json recent_developments; not yet in core_metrics (latest filed period is H1 FY2026). Component ratios (margins, lease, D&A, capex, WC, tax) are anchored to the FY2025 annual report, the latest filed annual.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted estimate at 30-Jun-2026: 261.286m ordinary shares at 31-Dec-2025 (H1 FY26 report, line 650, after 3.919m bought back for $9.949m) less ~6.1m shares for the ~$15.05m H2 FY26 buyback tranche (announced $25m of $30m executed by Aug-2026, at an assumed ~$2.45 average) = ~255.1m basic, plus 2.85m dilutive performance rights (FY25 diluted 268.056m less basic 265.205m). Held FLAT: SBC is immaterial and the dilutive rights are already in the count. Replace with the FY2026 annual report's cover-page and diluted-EPS figures when that filing is extracted.
inputs.net_debt_basis: GWA's own net debt definition (borrowings less cash, EXCLUDING AASB 16 lease liabilities) at 30-Jun-2026 as announced Aug-2026 ($127.9m, leverage 1.6x EBITDA). The latest FILED balance sheet (31-Dec-2025, H1 FY26) shows $96.0m on the same definition (borrowings 138.337 less cash 43.281 = 95.1 before capitalised borrowing costs). The H2 FY26 increase is ~$15m buyback (value-neutral, matched by the lower share count) plus ~$25-30m inventory pull-forward that management guides to unwind (FY27 cash conversion back to 80-85%); that unwind is NOT credited in the flows, which is deliberate conservatism. Using the Dec-2025 anchors instead (net debt 96.0, 264.1m diluted shares) would raise base IV by roughly $0.06/share.
inputs.debt_cash_date: 2025-12-31 (H1 FY26 balance sheet; components of the 30-Jun-2026 net debt are not in an extracted filing, so total_debt - cash here does not equal net_debt)
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report equity note: equity-settled share-based payment transactions $0.691m (FY24 $0.545m), ~0.15% of revenue. Treated as immaterial (0%) per the SBC-zero adaptation; the LTI performance rights are charged once via the diluted share count. House and street bases therefore coincide and band_position is null.
inputs.buyback_note: H1 FY26 on-market buyback $9.949m (3.919m shares) filed; a further ~$15m executed in H2 FY26 per the Aug-2026 result ($25m of the $30m program). The flat share count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-06-30 (net debt, announced Aug-2026); 2025-12-31 for filed debt/cash/lease components
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (estimated from 2025-12-31 filed count and the H2 FY26 buyback)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: 10y ACGB ~4.3% + 1.1 beta x 5.5% ERP = 10.4% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~6.0% (BBSW + margin), 4.2% after 30% tax; ~20% debt weight at market values -> 9.2%. Cyclicality and the FY27 soft-patch are priced in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked into WACC; the same 9.2% is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: B (leases as operating cost). Full lease cash (FY25: principal 12.311 + interest 1.587 = 13.898, 3.3% of revenue; H1 FY26 run-rate 2.9%) is charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities ($30.7m at Dec-2025) are EXCLUDED from net debt, matching GWA's own net debt definition. D&A for the tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY25 15.787 - 11.451 = 4.336, 1.0% of revenue). Reported normalised EBITDA (22.0% FY25) is post-AASB 16 and pre-lease, so the ebitda_margin_path is stated on that basis and the lease line brings it to ~18.8%.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported_fcf (FY25 OCF 69.151 - capex 2.836 = 66.315) - lease_cash 13.898 - sbc 0 - interest_income 0 = 52.417. Interest income ($1.2m) is NOT stripped because GWA is net-debt, not net-cash. reported_fcf is post interest paid (~$8m) so last_fcf is a levered owner FCF; the engine's flows are unlevered from EBIT. FY26 owner FCF (not filed) was roughly $25m on the 76% cash-conversion inventory build; FY22 (OCF 14.0) and FY19 (discontinued-ops gain) are excluded from any averaging.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, non-US cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations a1, b, e, f). Single-segment Bathrooms & Kitchens since the FY2018/19 Door & Access divestment; asset-light importer/distributor (capex ~1% of revenue) with Australia ~85% / UK ~9% / NZ ~7%. 10-year horizon because the base case carries a FY27 soft year and a FY29-31 cycle recovery before settling. Terminal value capped at 14x owner FCF (12x bear) - cyclical building-products distributor; the cap binds against Gordon at 9.2%/2.5% (15.3x). Price is the ASX regular close on the valuation date, not an after-hours print. The FY2026 annual report is not in the folder; when it is extracted, refile shares, net debt, cash, borrowings and lease cash from it.

bear.narrative: The housing/renovation downturn deepens through FY28 (volumes fall faster than the 5% price rise lifts revenue), Reece's private-label ranges (Milli, Posh) take share and squeeze pricing, NZ keeps shrinking, freight and a weak AUD outrun price recovery; EBITDA margin drops ~2.5pp to 19.5% before partly recovering to 20.5%. Cash conversion stays below target so the dividend/buyback pace slows. Terminal cap 12x reflects a structurally slower, share-losing distributor.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +1.5%: management says FY27 'resembles FY26' (+0.9%), with 5% AU / 4% NZ price rises against ~2% lower Australian building activity and some volume elasticity, UK still growing. FY29-31 3.0% as rate cuts lift renovation volumes off a low base; 2.5% nominal thereafter.
base.margin_rationale: Normalised EBITDA margin (pre-lease, post-AASB 16) has sat in a 21.6-23.1% band for six years (FY25 22.0%, FY26 ~22.3%). FY27 22.0% absorbs $3-4m extra ocean freight net of ~$3m FX hedge gain; drifts to 22.5% on cost discipline and mix. Lease cash 3.1% (FY25 3.3%, H1 FY26 run-rate 2.9%). D&A ex-ROU 1.0% = capex 1.0% (FY26 capex $4.3m). Cash tax 30% statutory (FY25 tax paid 20.7 on ~68 pre-tax = 30%). WC capture -20%: net working capital is ~18% of revenue (FY25 receivables 45.0 + inventory 90.6 - payables 60.3 = 75.3), so growth consumes cash.
base.narrative: GWA remains a low-growth, high-payout cash cow: revenue compounds at price plus a small volume recovery, margins hold in their historical band, and owner FCF runs ~$52-68m over the decade.

bull.narrative: Rate cuts revive Australian renovation and detached housing from FY28, price increases stick, UK keeps compounding at 6-7%, and Leak SmartShield / Smart Command add a recurring water-management stream; operating leverage lifts the EBITDA margin to the top of its historical band (23.1% FY20) and slightly beyond. No multiple expansion assumed: same 14x cap as base.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 25/50/25. Bear raised because GWA is a building-products cyclical whose own FY27 outlook is soft (Australian activity ~-2%, weaker H2 FY26 in renovation and the UK), net debt just rose to $127.9m (1.6x) and cash conversion missed the target band; the downside is margin and volume, not solvency, so it is not raised further. Bull lowered because it needs rate cuts, a housing recovery and new-product traction to coincide.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
